data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Mars Atmospheric Water Detector (MAWD)
record.description: The MAWD used an infrared grating spectrometer mounted on the orbiter scan platform that was boresighted with the television cameras and the IRTM. The instrument measured solar infrared radiation reflected from the surface through the atmosphere to the spacecraft. Spectral intervals were selected coincident with the wavelength of water-vapor absorption lines in the 1.4-micrometer band. The quantity of water vapor along the line of sight was measured from 1 to 100 micrometers of precipitable water with an accuracy of 5% or better. The instantaneous field of view of the instrument was 2 x 17 milliradians, and a stepping mirror rotated the line of sight through 15 positions to provide a roughly rectangular field of view of 17 x 31 milliradians. Operation of this experiment was terminated on August 7, 1980.
